newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee up in slow AM trade, Sept eyes $1,645.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee up in slow AM trade, Sept eyes $1,645.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were higher by the morning close on Friday on some light trade buying.
Traders said Sept/November switch trade was the only main feature and accounted for most of the volume of 989 lots.
Benchmark September gapped $21 higher and propelled to the session high of $1,617 per tonne towards the midsession. It ended $31 up at $1,610.
Third-month November was also $38 firmer at $1,608.
Traders said London's fortunes remained hinged on the New York arabica futures which have seen an encouraging turnaround from the recent spate of losses.
"New York is looking particularly good although the circumstances are different than in London," said one trader. "It will drag London up although the arb between the two will widen."
New York's September formed a double top at 184.50 cents a lb, a resistance which is proving difficult to break. A break at the level will ensure another 10 cent gain, the trader said.
Technically, London's September faces a key hurdle at $1,645 but there is a plenty of overhead resistance beyond that. Support is pegged around $1,545.
Weather-wise, Brazil's meteorologists Somar said a cold front with an intensity of 1024 would be in the Pacific Ocean on July 29 but it was still early to tell if it would pass Brazil's coffee areas.
"While this highlights that the frost risk has not yet gone away, 1024 is usually regarded as too weak to cause a frost," broker GNI said.
Another trader said: "A frost is still a concern but it's getting less by the day."
